note: Adversarial review complete. Found critical mechanical contradictions in distribution and OS portability, plus scope creep violating explicit North Star non-goals.

findings.topic: Bundle git history regeneration breaks pull-to-update
findings.message: Phase 4 mandates regenerating git history from scratch for every bundle. Phase 7 promises a 'natural pull-to-update path' for collaborators using git pull against the private remote. These are mechanically incompatible. If the bundle's history is regenerated from scratch on every release, the collaborator's local repository will share no commit ancestry with the updated remote, causing git pull to fail with a fatal unrelated histories error. You must either maintain a persistent scrubbed branch with continuous history, or abandon git pull for updates.

Phase 2 mandates 'parent-dir-fsync' for atomic writes as part of the OS-abstraction layer. While opening and fsyncing a parent directory is standard POSIX practice for ensuring a directory entry is durably written to disk, Windows Node.js does not permit this; attempting to fsync a directory handle natively throws an EPERM/EACCES error. This completely breaks the required durability primitives on one of the primary target OSes out of the gate.

Phase 3 enforces 'TLS-or-refuse' when binding to non-loopback interfaces, while simultaneously sanctioning Tailscale as the remote-access answer. Tailscale provides its own virtual IP (non-loopback) and handles end-to-end encryption natively. Forcing TLS on top of Tailscale requires the collaborator to provision a custom TLS certificate for their Tailscale IP. This introduces massive friction, contradicting the zero-friction onboarding goal, and will push users to abandon the sanctioned secure path.

findings.criterion: Non-goal: re-architecting the trio/foundry skills' internals
findings.message: Phase 6 plans to move the 10-minute status discipline out of the agent's prompts and into a timer-driven engine template. The North Star explicitly lists 're-architecting the trio/foundry skills internals' as a non-goal, and mandates 'identical agent behavior'. Removing the status reporting burden from the agent's cognitive loop alters its context and fundamentally re-architects how the trio operates internally. This must remain a prompt-driven convention.
